[ASSISTANT_SAID] Establish a consistent sleep schedule by going to bed and waking up at the same time every day, including weekends.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Create a calming pre-sleep routine that can include activities like reading, meditation, or a warm bath.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Optimize the sleep environment to be dark, quiet, and at a comfortable temperature.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Limit exposure to screens before bed to avoid blue light that can suppress melatonin production.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Get some morning sunlight to help regulate circadian rhythms.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Avoid snoozing and get out of bed as soon as the alarm goes off.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Engage in light physical activity in the morning to increase energy levels.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Eat a nutritious breakfast that includes protein, complex carbohydrates, and healthy fats.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Use a wake-up light that simulates a sunrise to wake up more naturally.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Make a plan for the morning to have a reason to get out of bed.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Limit caffeine and electronics before bedtime to improve sleep quality.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Aim for 7-9 hours of sleep each night to feel well-rested.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] It may take 1-2 weeks for the body to adjust to a new wake-up time.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Gradual adjustments to the wake-up time by 15-30 minutes every few days can help.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Consistency in wake-up time, even on weekends, will help the body adjust faster.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Regular exercise can improve sleep quality but should be avoided within 2-3 hours of bedtime.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Try progressive muscle relaxation to release tension before sleep.
